> I also noticed that there are no tests for side effects (this is not blocking):

v1 webhooks are only allowed to have `None` or `NoneOnDryRun` side effects (the distinction between those carries no behavior change, and is only informative). The `Unknown` and `Some` values were only for legacy webhooks using the `v1beta1` API prior to the introduction of the dry run concept.

> is there a better way (or a plan for a better way) to check if a webhook config is in effect?

the issue of knowing when a policy-driving object is effective (potentially across multiple API servers, and potentially across non-kube-apiservers that should not have write access to webhook config objects) is tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/54712

yes, I think this is good too. my only concern is whether we need clusterAdmin for this. is that the case?

Hoisting the answer to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/81857#discussion_r318224073 to the top level

Setup requires:
* read/write permissions to Deployment/Service/Secret objects, and read access to Endpoints (all of which are included in the default `edit` cluster role) to run the webhook pods and set up the relevant service
* read/write permissions on `{Mutating,Validating}WebhookConfiguration` objects (not included in any default role other than `cluster-admin`)
* read/write access to `CustomResourceDefinition` objects to declare a test type (not included in any default role other than `cluster-admin`)

Testing of the webhooks' efficacy requires:
* read/write permissions on pods/configmaps in the test namespaces (included in the default `edit` cluster role)
* read/write permissions on the test custom resource (not included in any default role other than `cluster-admin`)

> my only concern is whether we need clusterAdmin for this. is that the case?

admission configuration and custom resource definition APIs are cluster-admin-level operations, so it is expected that testing those things requires that level of permission

Ok. That specifically violates the conformance rules. One other thought -
are these tests disruptive if run in a production cluster? The webhooks
installed apply to all namespaces, IIRC.

This is looking like an instance where the rules may be too restrictive. I
wonder if we need a separate set of tests that can only be run in a test
cluster.

Ok, we need to revise the language in the criteria - there are already existing tests that require various levels of privilege. So we don’t want to strictly block on this. It is more around avoiding _unnecessary_ privileges. We need to provide the ability to segregate the tests based on privileges needed. 

Along those lines, it makes sense to tag these tests with a [Privileged:ClusterAdmin] tag (which is a new tag).

This is getting a little ahead of the policy but we can always tweak the tag later if the final policy is a bit different.
thanks @liggitt @johnbelamaric. I'm adding the [Privileged:ClusterAdmin] tag
rebased and promoted the discovery doc test https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82019, to cover all endpoints for conformance
/retest

Originally conformance was "make sure apps run on kube clusters the same".  We limited privilege because lots of clusters won't allow those privileges.  We want conformance to apply to more than just app function (to cover extension function and admin function).  We really, really, really need either profiles or to drop the requirements around non-privilege in the short term.

Edited for clarity
/retest

/lgtm

Note for conformance approvers: These tests require clusterAdmin, because this functionality is inherently privileged. To mitigate this in environments where the tests cannot be run as clusterAdmin, we added a [Privileged:ClusterAdmin] tag to that they can be easily excluded. This is a new tag and I will propose an update to the docs to cover this case.
/assign @bgrant0607 @smarterclayton

/approve

This is such a fundamental part of Kube that I think we should get it in conformance, then use this as a focus to sort out profiles.  You can be conformant for apps without allowing webhook registration, but you can't be conformant for extension without it.

AdmissionWebhook should have tests for all stable operations.
Those tests should go through the conformance process before being released.
This ticket is to help track what operations are yet to be covered by conformance tests.

## 15 Untested Stable Operations need Conformance Tests

These stable endpoints should be hit by e2e tests tagged with [conformance].
There are tests currently hitting 6 of the corresponding beta endpoints that could be updated to use stable.
Tests should be written to exercise the remaining 9 untested stable endpoints as well.

## 12 Tests that hit 6 out of 15 Beta Operations

These twelve tests could be updated to use the stable API, and subsequently promoted to conformance.
